# The lexicon — lexicon

> **RENDERED FROM STRUCTURED DATA — this page is not a markdown file.**
> Source: `lexicon/terms/pomdp-tensors.json` in `uni-cookbook` at `575fc93d9d31`.
> The sha256 recorded for this page is the digest of **that JSON**, not of this text. The
> renderer is `generators/derive_docs.cjs`; it copies fields and adds no facts. Every value
> below is a field of the source, verbatim, including the ones that read `NOT RUN` and `PENDING`.


The five-register lexicon file for the nine concepts whose domain is 'pomdp-tensors' in lexicon/CONCEPTS.json. Each entry renders ONE concept -- fixed by its definition, never by its English headword -- into Sanskrit, Latin, English, Hindi and Spanish, and records what each rendering gets WRONG alongside what it gets right. NOTHING HERE IS A CLAIM OF PERFECT TRANSLATION. Per rule 18.14 of the operator's charter ('Do not claim perfect translation'), every rendering here is PENDING until an independent back-translation test is RUN, and no test in this file has been run: no translator has been engaged and the reviewer field is NONE for all nine entries. Statuses record what was SEARCHED and FOUND on 2026-07-15 against the named authorities, including the negative results. This file raises no UNI rung, discharges no gate, and states no fact about nature.

*authored 2026-07-15 · reviewer: NONE - PENDING EXPERT REVIEW*

**Falsifiers for this file**

- Any register entry marked CITED whose quoted authority does not in fact carry that headword, or does not carry it in the sense claimed. That entry is a pseudopropheta and must be struck to PENDING-CITATION.
- Any COINED entry lacking its morphological derivation.
- Any back_translation_test reported as PASSED while reviewer remains 'NONE - PENDING EXPERT REVIEW'. No test in this file has been run; a PASS appearing without a named tester is a forgery.
- A register renders GENERATIVE_MODEL and GENERATIVE_PROCESS with one term (cross-domain; those concepts live in active-inference-math, but a tensor entry that blurs the model/process line trips the same wire).
- Any entry that lets a Sanskrit doctrinal term quietly assert a metaphysics -- e.g. rendering HIDDEN_STATE with avyakta (Samkhya's unmanifest prakrti) or E_TENSOR with vasana (karmic latency). The ambiguity_notes exist precisely to catch this and are the most load-bearing field in each entry.
- Any entry that treats the C tensor as learned, or the A/B/D/E tensors as set. The asymmetry is OBSERVED in the corpus (01-kitchen-rules M13: learning covers A/B/D/E, never C) and a register that loses it has lost the concept.
- A status field holds anything other than one bare token from {CITED, PENDING-CITATION, COINED, NOT-ATTEMPTED}, or a mixed rendering is graded at the strength of its strongest member rather than its weakest. Run the enum validator in this file's header comment; a compound of cited members is COINED, never CITED.

## POMDP — 

*Store:* `TRUE` · *Confidence:* `LOW for Sanskrit and Latin (both wholesale coinages for a 20th-century formalism; the Latin observabilis trap and the Sanskrit nirṇaya 'completeness' conflict are unrepaired). MEDIUM for Spanish (established calque, unsourced). LOW for Hindi (unsourced). HIGH only for English, which is the concept's own label and not a translation.` · *Reviewer:* `NONE - PENDING EXPERT REVIEW`

A discrete formalism of hidden states, observations and actions in which states are not directly visible, over which this corpus's engine runs the loop perceive, EFE-plan, act, learn.

| register | form | literal gloss | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| sanskrit | अंशतःप्रत्यक्षा मार्कोव-निर्णय-प्रक्रिया (aṃśataḥ-pratyakṣā mārkova-nirṇaya-prakriyā) | a Markov decision-procedure, perceptible in part | COINED |
| latin | PROCESSUS DECISIONIS MARKOVIANUS PARTIM OBSERVABILIS | a Markovian process of decision, observable in part | COINED |
| english | partially observable Markov decision process | A discrete formalism of hidden states, observations and actions in which the states are not directly visible, so that an agent must act from a belief over states rather than from the states themselves; the formalism over which this corpus's engine runs perceive, EFE-plan, act, learn. | — |
| hindi | आंशिक रूप से प्रेक्षणीय मार्कोव निर्णय प्रक्रिया () | partially observable Markov decision process | PENDING-CITATION |
| spanish | proceso de decisión de Márkov parcialmente observable | partially observable Markov decision process | PENDING-CITATION |

**Ambiguity notes**

- THE MOST DANGEROUS WORD IN THE LATIN IS observabilis. L&S glosses it 'remarkable, observable' and marks it post-Augustan, and its attested uses do not mean 'capable of being observed' in the technical sense of observability theory. The Vulgate citation L&S gives -- Exod. 12.42, 'nox ista est observabilis Domini' -- means 'this is the night TO BE KEPT/celebrated of the Lord', i.e. a night to be religiously OBSERVED. Latin observo carries both 'to watch/note' and 'to keep/observe (a rite, a law)', and observabilis inherits the second. To a Latinist, PARTIM OBSERVABILIS therefore risks reading 'partly remarkable' or 'partly to-be-ritually-kept'. The word is retained for want of a better deverbative, but this trap is live and is the first thing a reviewer should attack.
- 'Partially observable' is the load-bearing qualifier (CONCEPTS.json) and the reason a recognition density is needed at all. A register that drops 'partim'/'aṃśataḥ' does not name a weaker version of the concept -- it names a DIFFERENT formalism (a plain MDP), in which no belief state and no inference are required. The qualifier is not decoration.
- Sanskrit nirṇaya [MW 555,1] leads with 'COMPLETE ascertainment'. That is precisely what a partially observable process denies: in a POMDP the ascertainment is constitutively incomplete. The compound therefore sets its own qualifier fighting its own head noun. This is recorded rather than repaired because every alternative considered was worse; it is the single weakest joint in the Sanskrit entry.
- nirṇaya further carries legal 'sentence, verdict' and logical 'deduction, inference' senses [MW 555,1]. The decision in a POMDP is an action selection under uncertainty -- neither a juridical verdict nor a deductive conclusion.
- Sanskrit prakriyā [MW 653] carries 'a ceremony, observance, formality' and 'a chapter (esp. the introductory chapter of a work)'. A POMDP is neither a rite nor a book-division. Note the accidental rhyme with the Latin trap above: BOTH registers' words for the process/observing drift toward RITUAL OBSERVANCE. That is a coincidence of two independent lexicons, not evidence of anything, and must not be presented as a finding.
- Latin decisio is literally 'a cutting off' (from decīdo) and its figurative sense II is 'a decision, SETTLEMENT, AGREEMENT' -- Cicero's uses are of legal settlements between parties. A POMDP decision is not negotiated and has no counterparty.
- 'Markov' names a person and imports nothing but the memorylessness property. No register may gloss it descriptively (e.g. as 'memoryless'), because the concept is fixed to the formalism's conventional name, and a descriptive gloss would silently assert which property is meant.

**Forbidden mistranslations**

| register | form | why it is wrong |
|---|---|---|
|  |  | Puts Markovianae in agreement with decisionis. It is the process that carries the Markov property, not the decision. A grammatically fluent error that inverts the formalism. |
|  |  | Yields a Markov decision process -- a different and strictly easier formalism, with no hidden state, no belief, and no need for inference. This is not a translation of the concept but a replacement of it. |
|  |  | gūḍha [MW 360,3] means 'covered, hidden, concealed, invisible, SECRET, PRIVATE'. It would assert that the process is clandestine. See HIDDEN_STATE. |
|  |  | 'observado' (observed) for 'observable'. The states are not partly observed; they are partly OBSERVABLE -- a modal claim about what could be seen, not a report of what was. |

**Back-translation test** — status: `NOT YET RUN -- no translator engaged. Any PASS recorded here without a named tester is a forgery.`

Give an independent translator competent in the register ONLY the rendering, with this file's definition withheld. Ask: 'What object does this term denote? Answer in English in one sentence.'

## A_TENSOR — 

*Store:* `TRUE` · *Confidence:* `LOW. Both learned registers are coinages for an object neither lexicon knows, the Spanish rests on a convention its own dictionary does not record, and the Hindi is unsourced. The one thing here held with confidence is a NEGATIVE: verisimilitudo is decisively wrong, and that is evidenced.` · *Reviewer:* `NONE - PENDING EXPERT REVIEW`

The tensor encoding p(o|s), mapping hidden states to observations, and one of the four tensors this corpus's engine learns by conjugate-Dirichlet counts.

| register | form | literal gloss | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| sanskrit | A-प्रदिश (A-pradiśa) | the A-tensor (lit., by MW's attested sense, 'the A-indication/direction' -- which is NOT what is meant) | COINED |
| latin | TENSOR A | the A-stretcher / the A-tensor | COINED |
| english | A tensor (likelihood) | The tensor encoding p(o\|s) -- the probability of each observation given each hidden state -- which maps hidden states to observations and is one of the four tensors (A, B, D, E) that this corpus's engine learns by conjugate-Dirichlet counts. | — |
| hindi | A-प्रदिश () | the A tensor | PENDING-CITATION |
| spanish | tensor A (verosimilitud) | the A tensor (likelihood) | PENDING-CITATION |

**Ambiguity notes**

- THE CENTRAL TRAP OF THIS ENTRY: a likelihood is NOT a probability of the hidden state. p(o|s) read as a function of s is not a distribution over s and does not normalise over s. Every register word here that means 'how probable the state is' or 'how true it is' names a different object -- the posterior, or worse, a truth-value.
- This is why Latin verisimilitudo is fatal and not merely infelicitous. L&S does not even grant it an independent entry; the headword reads 'vērĭsĭmĭlis, vērĭsĭmĭlĭter, and vērĭsĭmĭlĭtūdo, more correctly written separately, vērī simĭlis, etc., v. under verus and similis' -- i.e. the word IS 'veri similis', LIKE THE TRUTH. It asserts likeness-to-truth, which is exactly the assertion a likelihood does not make.
- SPANISH AND LATIN DIVERGE HERE, AND THE DIVERGENCE MUST NOT BE LAUNDERED. Spanish has conventionalised 'verosimilitud' for statistical likelihood; Latin has not. The Spanish convention is a fait accompli of usage and is admissible in Spanish on those terms. It may NOT be back-borrowed into Latin on the strength of the cognate: the Latin word's attested semantics actively contradict the concept. A translator who reasons 'Spanish says verosimilitud, so Latin says verisimilitudo' has produced a pseudopropheta by cognate.
- Sanskrit pradiś [MW 679,3] carries 'order, command, dominion'. The A tensor commands nothing and has dominion over nothing. These senses are wholly absent from the concept and are live in the attested word.
- tantra [MW 436,1-2] is the tempting etymological parallel: MW gives 'a loom', 'the warp', and 'the leading or principal or essential part, main point, characteristic feature, model, type, system, framework'. The loom/warp sense is a genuine semantic cousin of Latin tendo's 'stretch'. It is nevertheless FORBIDDEN (below), because MW's same entry gives 'a class of works teaching magical and mystical formularies'. Using tantra would import the entire Tantric corpus into a likelihood matrix.
- CONCEPTS.json: 'ambiguity lives in A, controllability lives in B'. A register that renders A and B with interchangeable words for 'matrix/array' loses the division of labour that makes the pair mean anything.
- The parenthetical '(likelihood)' is a gloss of the tensor's ROLE, not part of its name. The name is the letter A (SD-01). A register that translates 'likelihood' and drops the A has named the role and lost the object.

**Forbidden mistranslations**

| register | form | why it is wrong |
|---|---|---|
|  |  | L&S analyses the word as vērī simĭlis, 'like the truth'. It asserts probability-of-being-true. A likelihood is not the probability that the state is true; it is the probability of the DATUM given the state. This inverts the conditional. |
|  |  | TWO independent failures. (1) MW [1179,1] gives 'imagination, supposition, assumption (also as a rhet. figure...)' and does NOT carry 'probability' -- the authority does not license the sense. (2) Even if it did, 'probability' is the wrong object: likelihood is not a probability over states. The modern Hindi सम्भावना = probability is a later development and cannot be retrojected onto MW. |
|  |  | Etymologically apt (MW 436: 'a loom', 'the warp' -- the stretch-sense that also gives Latin tensor), and doctrinally catastrophic: MW's same entry gives 'a class of works teaching magical and mystical formularies'. Imports the Tantric corpus wholesale. A metaphysics smuggled in on an etymology is the exact failure CONCEPTS.json warns of. |
|  |  | Violates SD-01. A is an arbitrary index, not an ordinal. A is the likelihood; it is first in nothing. The letters are conventional labels, not abbreviations. |

But the re-read of the full p. 589 entry found (i) a fourth denied sense, 'past, completed', which the previous rating did not know about and which points at the live/current state s in exactly the wrong direction, and (ii) adverbial forms glossing 'secretly', 'behind one's back', 'without the knowledge of' -- the agentive-concealment implicature for which this very entry rejects gūḍha. The entry was rating its own word against a standard it had not applied to it. The two registers are NOT equally grounded and the previous rating implied they were: Latin excludes the concealer by grammar, Sanskrit only by sense-selection. The Advaita parokṣa-jñāna freight remains flagged and unverified, so it contributes nothing to either rating.` · *Reviewer:* `NONE - PENDING EXPERT REVIEW`

The quantity s that an agent cannot observe directly and must infer, and about which the recognition density is a belief.

| register | form | literal gloss | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| sanskrit | परोक्षावस्था (parokṣāvasthā) | a state beyond the range of sight | COINED |
| latin | STATUS LATENS | a state that lies hidden | COINED |
| english | hidden state | The quantity s that an agent cannot observe directly and must therefore infer, and about which the recognition density is a belief. | — |
| hindi | प्रच्छन्न अवस्था () | hidden state | PENDING-CITATION |
| spanish | estado oculto | hidden state | PENDING-CITATION |

**Ambiguity notes**

- THE CONCEPT'S OWN NOTE IS THE FENCE: CONCEPTS.json states "'Hidden' means not directly observable, NOT concealed, secret, or withheld by anyone." There is no agent doing the hiding. Every register has an obvious word for 'hidden' that smuggles a concealer in, and choosing between them is the entire work of this entry.
- WHY LATIN latens AND NOT occultus: lateō is marked 'v. n.' in L&S -- verb NEUTER, i.e. intransitive. It means 'to lie hid' as something the subject does, or rather undergoes, with no agent. occultus and absconditus are participles of occulō and abscondō, transitive verbs of actively hiding, and both therefore imply someone who hid the thing. The grammar of the Latin verb, not a stylistic preference, is what selects latens.
- parokṣa's OWN GLOSS CONTAINS FOUR SENSES THE CONCEPT DENIES. MW [589]: 'beyond the range of sight, invisible, ABSENT, UNKNOWN, unintelligible', and -- found only on the adversarial re-read of 2026-07-15 -- 'PAST, COMPLETED'. The hidden state is NOT absent -- it is present and doing causal work, which is why it can be inferred at all. It is not unknown in principle -- it is precisely what the recognition density is a belief ABOUT. 'Unintelligible' is worse still: an unintelligible state could not be inferred. And 'past, completed' is worse than all three: s is the CURRENT hidden state, live at time t and causing o right now; a word that reads 'the completed state' names something finished and gone, which is the one thing s must not be. The count in this note previously read 'two' in its heading and 'three' in its body, and both were wrong: the best-attested Sanskrit word carries FOUR wrong senses alongside its one right one.
- THE SECRECY OBJECTION THIS ENTRY RAISES AGAINST गूढ APPLIES TO ITS OWN CHOSEN WORD, AND THAT WAS MISSED UNTIL THE ADVERSARIAL RE-READ. This entry rejects gūḍha because MW [360,3] gives 'SECRET, PRIVATE' -- i.e. it posits a concealer, which the concept forbids. But MW's parokṣa entry [589] carries, in its own adverbial forms: parokṣeṇa 'out of sight, SECRETLY, mysteriously'; parokṣāt 'SECRETLY, without the knowledge of'; parokṣam 'out of sight, BEHIND ONE'S BACK, in the absence or WITHOUT THE KNOWLEDGE OF'; parokṣe 'BEHIND THE BACK OF'. 'Behind one's back' and 'without the knowledge of' are not merely secrecy-adjacent -- they are agentive: they presuppose a party FROM WHOM something is kept. That is the precise implicature the concept's own fence forbids ('NOT concealed, secret, or withheld by anyone') and the precise ground on which this entry rejects gūḍha. The defence available is narrow and must not be overstated: the ADJECTIVE parokṣa in its lead sense is agent-neutral ('beyond the range of sight'), and it is the adjective, not the adverbs, that enters parokṣāvasthā. But the adverbial senses are in the same entry, they are the forms a reader meets most often in texts, and they establish that Sanskrit parokṣa is NOT the clean agent-free word this entry represented it as. The Latin rendering has a real structural defence here that the Sanskrit does not: lateō's intransitivity is a GRAMMATICAL fact about the verb that excludes an agent, whereas parokṣa's agent-neutrality is only a fact about which sense one selects. STATUS LATENS is therefore better grounded than parokṣāvasthā, and this entry previously implied they were equally strong.
- parokṣa carries Advaita epistemological freight: parokṣa-jñāna (mediate/indirect knowledge) is opposed to aparokṣa-jñāna (immediate knowledge), and the pair is technical in Vedanta. Using parokṣa may import a theory of mediate cognition. [Freight claim NOT verified against MW/Apte this session -- flagged suspicion, not citation. Falsifier: read MW s.v. parokṣa-jñāna and aparokṣa.]
- avasthā [MW 106,1] carries 'appearance (in a court of justice)' and, per MW, 'the female organs of generation' in specific textual contexts. Neither is in the concept; both are in the entry.
- LATIN status's SENSE I IS BODILY. L&S I.A: 'mode or way of standing, of holding one's body (at rest), posture, position, attitude, station, carriage'; I.C 'size, height, stature'. The concept needs sense II ('condition, state'). A posture-reading is not merely odd here -- it lands the term on the wrong side of the WORLD/BODY/MIND typing (M12), where hidden states are MIND-side inferential objects and postures are BODY-side interoceptive ones.
- L&S carries a second, participial status ('set, fixed, appointed, regular', from sisto). STATUS LATENS is largely protected from this reading by latens, but the homonym is live in the bare word and matters for D_TENSOR.
- SPANISH AND LATIN DIVERGE, AS THEY DID FOR verosimilitud. Spanish 'estado oculto' is the settled term of art despite 'oculto' descending from occulō and carrying exactly the concealment implicature Latin occultus is rejected for. Usage has bleached the Spanish word; it has not bleached the Latin one. A translator may NOT reason from 'estado oculto' back to STATUS OCCULTUS -- that is the pseudopropheta-by-cognate move, the same error as verisimilitudo, and this file rejects it in both directions.

**Forbidden mistranslations**

| register | form | why it is wrong |
|---|---|---|
|  |  | MW [360,3]: 'gUQa mfn. covered, hidden, concealed, invisible, SECRET, PRIVATE, RV. &c.', with 'disguised' in a sub-entry (Manu, MBh.). Asserts secrecy and disguise -- someone has hidden something. The concept's note forbids exactly this: not concealed, secret, or withheld by anyone. |
|  |  | Both are participles of TRANSITIVE verbs of hiding (occulō, abscondō) and so posit a concealer. The concept has none. Contrast lateō, marked 'v. n.' in L&S -- intransitive, no agent. [The L&S entries for occultus and absconditus were NOT read this session; the claim rests on the transitivity of their base verbs. Falsifier: read both entries.] |
|  |  | REJECTED on doctrinal-freight grounds: in Samkhya, avyakta names the unmanifest prakṛti/pradhāna -- primordial undifferentiated matter -- so the word would make the hidden state an item of Samkhya cosmology. NOTE THE EVIDENCE GRADE: NOT verified against MW this session; flagged suspicion, not citation. Falsifier: read MW s.v. avyakta. |
|  |  | Means secret/mystery -- and in many contexts an esoteric doctrine. Asserts both secrecy and initiatory withholding. [NOT verified against MW this session -- flagged suspicion.] |
|  |  | Asserts secrecy outright. Note this is NOT an objection to the established 'estado oculto', which usage has bleached; 'secreto' has not been bleached and reintroduces the concealer. |
|  |  | The state is inferable -- that is the entire premise. parokṣa's 'unknown, unintelligible' senses [MW 589] drift this way and must be fenced off. A state that could not be known could not be the object of a recognition density. |

**Back-translation test** — status: `NOT YET RUN -- no translator engaged.`

Give an independent translator ONLY the rendering, definition withheld. Ask: (1) 'What does this denote?' (2) 'Is anyone hiding it?' (3) 'Can it be known?' (4) 'Is the thing it denotes happening now, or is it finished and past?'

## OBSERVATION — 

*Store:* `TRUE` · *Confidence:* `LOW-to-MEDIUM. The comparative that previously stood here -- 'lower than HIDDEN_STATE' -- is WITHDRAWN: the adversarial re-read of 2026-07-15 downgraded HIDDEN_STATE's Sanskrit to LOW-to-MEDIUM as well, so the two Sanskrit renderings now sit at the same grade and this entry is no longer the lower of the pair. Attestation is not admissibility: pratyakṣa is attested exactly as claimed [MW 674,2] -- re-confirmed verbatim under audit, parenthetical included, and it remains the only fully CITED headword-in-sense in this file -- and it may still be inadmissible, because MW's own noun gloss 'ocular EVIDENCE' asserts probative force that o does not have, before the unverified Nyāya-pramāṇa objection is even reached. That gap -- CITED, re-confirmed, yet possibly forbidden -- is the most important thing in this entry, and the audit widened it rather than closing it: the evidentiary objection got STRONGER (it is now lexical, not merely doctrinal) at the same time as the citation got firmer. Attestation and admissibility moved in opposite directions on the same re-read, which is precisely why the file keeps them as two tests. The reason the domain's two best-attested Sanskrit words may both have to be re-cut together is unchanged and now better evidenced on both sides.` · *Reviewer:* `NONE - PENDING EXPERT REVIEW`

The quantity o that actually arrived at the sensor, which is what a belief is scored against and what a receipt records.

| register | form | literal gloss | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| sanskrit | प्रत्यक्ष (pratyakṣa) | present before the eyes; that which is present before the eyes | CITED |
| latin | OBSERVATUM | the thing observed; a thing that has been noted | COINED |
| english | observation | The quantity o that actually arrived at the sensor -- what a belief is scored against, and what a receipt records. | — |
| hindi | प्रेक्षण () | observation | PENDING-CITATION |
| spanish | observación | observation | PENDING-CITATION |

**Ambiguity notes**

- THE ACT/DATUM SPLIT IS THE FIRST TRAP AND IT CATCHES THREE REGISTERS. The concept is the QUANTITY o that arrived -- a datum, a thing. It is not the act of observing. Latin observatio, Spanish observación and Hindi प्रेक्षण all name the act primarily (Spanish softens this with 'accion Y EFECTO de'). This is why the Latin here is OBSERVATUM (the thing observed) and not observatio, and it is the one place in this file where the coined form is clearly better than the attested alternative.
- THE PRAMĀṆA PROBLEM, AND IT MAY BE FATAL TO THE SANSKRIT. In Nyāya, pratyakṣa is the first of the pramāṇas -- the MEANS OF VALID KNOWLEDGE. The word does not merely name a percept; in its technical use it certifies the percept as veridical. But o is 'the quantity that ACTUALLY ARRIVED at the sensor' -- arrival, not validity. A sensor can deliver a corrupt, noisy, or miscalibrated reading and it is still o; that is precisely why the A tensor is needed and why ambiguity lives in A. Rendering OBSERVATION as pratyakṣa therefore risks asserting that every observation is valid knowledge -- a metaphysical claim the corpus must not make, and one that would quietly dissolve the whole point of a likelihood. This is the exact hazard CONCEPTS.json names ('Sanskrit philosophical vocabulary carries DOCTRINAL FREIGHT... no translation choice may quietly assert a metaphysics') and the operator's charter names ('Do not assume Sanskrit automatically prevents ambiguity'). The Nyāya-pramāṇa claim is NOT verified against MW or a Nyāya source this session -- it is flagged, not cited. Falsifier: read MW s.v. pramāṇa and a Nyāya-sūtra reference on pratyakṣa as pramāṇa. If confirmed, the CITED status above stands for the word but the rendering may still have to be struck on freight grounds -- attestation and admissibility are different tests, and passing the first does not pass the second. UPDATE, ADVERSARIAL RE-READ 2026-07-15: the objection is now PARTLY GROUNDED IN MW ITSELF and no longer rests solely on the unverified Nyāya claim. The re-read of [674,2] found noun senses the entry had not recorded, among them 'OCULAR EVIDENCE, direct perception, apprehension by the senses'. 'Evidence' is an evidentiary/probative word: it says the percept ESTABLISHES something. o establishes nothing -- it is what arrived, veridical or not, and a corrupt sensor reading is still o. So the validity implicature this note feared is visible in MW's plain lexical glosses, without any appeal to Nyāya. State the evidence grades separately and do not merge them: the LEXICAL evidentiary sense is now CITED [MW 674,2]; the NYĀYA-pramāṇa doctrinal claim remains UNVERIFIED and flagged. The first is sufficient on its own to keep the rendering under examination. The re-read also found 'superintendence of, care for' -- a supervisory sense wholly absent from the concept; o supervises nothing.
- pratyakṣa's LEXICAL SENSE IS OCULAR ('present before the EYES', MW 674,2; the word is literally prati + akṣa, 'before the eye'). o is whatever arrived at ANY sensor -- a thermometer reading, a byte count, an interoceptive hardware signal (M12). The register word is narrower than the concept in modality and would have to be stretched.
- THE BRIDGE NOTE, WHICH IS THIS CONCEPT'S REASON FOR EXISTING: CONCEPTS.json says o in an equation and a receipt in a ledger are 'the same kind of object, which is why a confabulated observation corrupts the model rather than merely embarrassing the author'. Any register that renders o as a mere 'impression', 'appearance', or 'sense-datum' -- something mental and private -- severs that bridge. The word must be able to denote a LOGGED, EXTERNAL, CHECKABLE thing, because a receipt is one.
- Latin observō carries 'to watch FOR, seek to catch' [L&S] -- purposive, anticipatory watching. o is passive arrival; nothing is sought. The verb also carries the 'keep/observe a rite or law' sense that makes observabilis so treacherous in POMDP.
- OBSERVATION is the counterpart of HIDDEN_STATE and the lexicon already knows it: MW defines praty-akṣa expressly as 'opp. to parokṣa'. Whatever this entry finally settles on, it must remain the antonym of whatever HIDDEN_STATE settles on. If pratyakṣa is struck on pramāṇa grounds, parokṣāvasthā loses its lexicographic anchor and BOTH entries must be re-cut together.

**Forbidden mistranslations**

| register | form | why it is wrong |
|---|---|---|
|  |  | L&S gives 'an observing, watching' -- the ACT. The concept is the DATUM that arrived. Rendering the act for the thing makes o a process rather than a quantity, and a process cannot be what a belief is scored against. |
|  |  | Names a MEANS OF VALID KNOWLEDGE. It asserts validity, which o does not have and does not need -- o is what arrived, veridical or not. This is the sharpest form of the pramāṇa problem and the reason it must be fenced even for pratyakṣa. |
|  |  | Names sight/the faculty of seeing (and, in Buddhist usage, a VIEW in the doctrinal sense -- micchā-dṛṣṭi, 'wrong view'). Names the faculty or a doctrine, not the datum. [NOT verified against MW this session -- flagged suspicion.] |
|  |  | Makes o mental and private. o must be able to be a LOGGED external quantity -- a receipt -- because CONCEPTS.json makes the equation's o and the ledger's receipt the same kind of object. A private impression cannot be a receipt. |
|  |  | o is what ARRIVED, not what is the case. A corrupt sensor reading is still o. Any validity-word collapses the distinction between the observation and the hidden state it is evidence about -- which is the distinction the entire domain is built on. |

**Back-translation test** — status: `NOT YET RUN -- no translator engaged.`

Give an independent translator ONLY the rendering, definition withheld. Ask: (1) 'Does this denote an act or a thing?' (2) 'Does it imply the thing is true or valid?' (3) 'Could this word denote a number written into a log by a machine?'

# natura-biology — lexicon

> **RENDERED FROM STRUCTURED DATA — this page is not a markdown file.**
> Source: `lexicon/terms/natura-biology.json` in `uni-cookbook` at `575fc93d9d31`.
> The sha256 recorded for this page is the digest of **that JSON**, not of this text. The
> renderer is `generators/derive_docs.cjs`; it copies fields and adds no facts. Every value
> below is a field of the source, verbatim, including the ones that read `NOT RUN` and `PENDING`.



*authored 2026-07-15 · reviewer: NONE - PENDING EXPERT REVIEW. An adversarial CITATION AUDIT (not an expert review) was run 2026-07-15 -- see adversarial_audit_2026_07_15. It checked the authorities; it did NOT check the Sanskrit or Latin competence of the renderings, and it is not a substitute for the expert review still owed.*

**Falsifiers for this file**

- Any Sanskrit or Latin headword below is shown not to exist in the cited authority, or not to carry the sense in which this file quotes it. That entry is a pseudopropheta and must be struck to PENDING-CITATION.
- Any entry marked CITED is shown to rest on a sense the authority does not carry.
- Any COINED entry is shown to have an attested classical equivalent that was missed. The coinage must then be withdrawn in favour of the attestation.
- Any back_translation_test below is RUN and FAILS. Every test in this file is NOT-RUN; no register here has passed anything.
- Any entry is shown to render a TRUE-store concept with a term that asserts an experiencer, a soul, or a metaphysics the definition withholds.
- A domain value other than 'natura' appears in any entry of this file.
- Any quotation of an authority in this file is shown to be TRIMMED, re-attributed, or otherwise shaped so as to make a register look better-attested than the authority supports. This falsifier was ADDED 2026-07-15 after an adversarial audit found six such defects, all running in that one direction (see adversarial_audit_2026_07_15). The original falsifier list guarded only against INVENTED entries; it did not guard against motivated quotation of real ones, which is the defect this file actually had.

## CELL — 

*Store:* `TRUE` · *Domain:* `natura` · *Confidence:* `Sanskrit: headword read, claimed sense REFUTED by the authority -- coinage stands or falls on expert review. Latin: form read and carried, biological sense read and ABSENT. Hindi: read negative in Platts, unsourced otherwise. Spanish: unsourced. Overall: LOW. The most valuable content in this entry is the gap between the modern word and what the 1899 and 1879 authorities actually say.` · *Reviewer:* `NONE - PENDING EXPERT REVIEW`

The design unit of biology and the canonical Markov blanket, plasma-membrane bounded and dominated by viscosity and diffusion at Re of order 1e-5.

| register | form | literal gloss | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| sanskrit | कोशिका (kosika) | little vessel; little container | COINED |
| latin | cellula | a small store-room; a little chamber | CITED (form only, NOT the biological sense) |
| english | cell | The design unit of biology and the canonical Markov blanket, plasma-membrane bounded and dominated by viscosity and diffusion at Re of order 1e-5. | — |
| hindi | कोशिका () | cell (biological) -- the author's working knowledge, UNSOURCED | PENDING-CITATION |
| spanish | celula (célula) | cell (biological) -- the author's working knowledge, UNSOURCED | PENDING-CITATION |

**Ambiguity notes**

- kośa/kośikā is a CONTAINER word. Its whole attested field is vessel, cask, box, sheath, scabbard, pod, nut-shell, cocoon. It therefore imports the image of a hollow thing whose interesting property is that it holds something. A cell is not primarily a container: the definition's load-bearing property is the BOUNDARY and its conditional independence, not the volume enclosed.
- THE HEAVIEST FREIGHT IN THIS FILE: MW s.v. कोश explicitly carries 'the three sheaths' as a Vedanta technical sense (authority: Vedāntas.). This is the pancakosa doctrine, in which the kosas are the sheaths ENVELOPING THE ATMAN. Rendering 'cell' as kośa/kośikā to a reader trained in Vedanta says that a cell is a sheath around a self. That asserts exactly the metaphysics the corpus withholds, and it does so invisibly, because the word looks like a neutral technical term.
- MW s.v. कोश also gives 'a dictionary, lexicon or vocabulary'. A word meaning 'lexicon' is a poor choice of headword INSIDE a lexicon file: kośa is the standard Sanskrit word for the genre this very file belongs to (cf. Amarakosa). The collision is real and will confuse readers of this document specifically.
- MW s.v. कोश carries anatomical senses that are near-misses and therefore dangerous. CORRECTED 2026-07-15 BY ADVERSARIAL RE-READ: an earlier version of this note attributed all five to 'L.' That blanket attribution was FALSE and has been struck. MW's actual authorities, re-read at getword.php?key=koSa: 'the membrane covering an egg (in the womb)' -- Suśr.; VarBṛ.; MārkP. (NOT L.); 'a testicle or the scrotum' -- Suśr.; VarBṛS. (NOT L.); 'the penis' -- W. (Wilson, NOT L.); 'the vulva' -- L.; 'an egg' -- L. Only two of the five are L. THE CORRECTION CUTS AGAINST THE AUTHOR AND SHARPENS THE WARNING: kośa's anatomical senses are NOT lexicographers-only curiosities, they are attested in Suśruta -- the classical medical corpus itself. A reader may therefore take kośa as already-anatomical, ON GOOD LITERARY EVIDENCE, and conclude the biological sense is attested. It is attested for THOSE organs, in medicine, and NOT for the cell. The false '(all L.)' had made this trap look smaller than it is.
- Latin cellula imports a SMALL ROOM: the monastic and domestic register. A room is a negative space defined by its walls; the concept's boundary is an active, selectively permeable, physically-constituted surface. The metaphor inverts which part is the object.
- The definition calls the cell 'the canonical Markov blanket'. Read this WITH the MEMBRANE entry: 'canonical' names the standard EXAMPLE, and does not mean I(mu;eta|b) was ever estimated for a cell. It was not. No register may be chosen so as to make the blanket claim sound settled.
- Re of order 1e-5 is a scope, not a decoration: it fixes the cell in the viscous regime. A rendering that ports the word to a macroscopic 'chamber' loses the only property that makes the physics of the referent what it is.

**Forbidden mistranslations**

| register | form | why it is wrong |
|---|---|---|
|  |  | Imports an animating soul and, in Jain and Vedantic usage, a transmigrating self. The concept is a membrane-bounded physical unit. This asserts an experiencer where the definition names none, and it is the single most attractive wrong answer because 'cell' and 'living thing' feel adjacent in English. |
|  |  | Wrong rung of the scale ladder by roughly five orders of magnitude, and it imports Vaisesika atomism. A cell is not a minimal particle; it is a bounded system with interior dynamics. |
|  |  | L&S s.v. cella gives, alongside the storeroom sense, 'The part of a temple in which the image of a god stood, the chapel' (II. A.), an apartment in a bathing-house (II. B.), the chamber of servants and slaves, and a room in a brothel (II. D., Petr.; Juv.). Every one of those registers is imported with the word. LAST SENTENCE STRUCK 2026-07-15 AS REFUTED BY THE CITED AUTHORITY: it read 'The diminutive cellula at least narrows to the store-room, which is why the diminutive and not the parent is proposed.' L&S s.v. cellula explicitly carries 'acc. to cella, II. D., Petr. 11, 1' -- the brothel sense passes straight into the diminutive. cellula escapes the temple and bath senses, not the brothel one. That is a smaller argument for the diminutive than this file made, and the smaller one is the true one. |
|  |  | L&S was read and REFUTES this: it carries only 'a small store-room or apartment' (Ter.; Col.). Presenting the biological sense as classical fabricates an attestation that the authority does not contain. |
|  |  | MW was read and REFUTES this: 'koSikA f. a drinking-vessel, L.' The headword is real; the sense is modern. This is the exact shape of the pseudopropheta the brief warns against -- a real headword carrying a sense its authority never gave it. |

**Back-translation test** — status: `NOT-RUN`

## MEMBRANE — 

*Store:* `TRUE` · *Domain:* `natura` · *Confidence:* `Latin: the best-attested register in this file -- headword read, COVERING sense carried, marked classical by L&S, Cicero cited; the concept's defining sense (lipid, selectively permeable) read for and ABSENT. 'Sense carried' was struck 2026-07-15 as ambiguous between those two and read as the second. Sanskrit: tvac read and carried in the covering sense, silent on every defining property. Hindi: unsourced, and the obvious candidate was read and refuted in the classical register. Spanish: unsourced. Overall: MEDIUM for Latin topology, LOW for the concept's actual discriminating properties, which NO register here carries.` · *Reviewer:* `NONE - PENDING EXPERT REVIEW`

A selectively permeable lipid boundary, which is a surface for reasons of lipid physics and history, and whose satisfying I(mu;eta|b) = 0 is a DIFFERENT question whose answer is NOT-MEASURED.

| register | form | literal gloss | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| sanskrit | त्वच् (tvac) | skin; hide; bark; a covering | CITED (as 'covering/skin' -- NOT as 'lipid bilayer') |
| latin | membrana | the skin or membrane covering parts of the body | CITED (as 'the skin or membrane that covers parts of the body' -- NOT as 'a selectively permeable LIPID boundary') |
| english | membrane | A selectively permeable lipid boundary, which is a surface for reasons of lipid physics and history, and whose satisfying I(mu;eta\|b) = 0 is a DIFFERENT question whose answer is NOT-MEASURED. | — |
| hindi | झिल्ली () | membrane -- the author's working knowledge, UNSOURCED | PENDING-CITATION |
| spanish | membrana | membrane -- the author's working knowledge, UNSOURCED | PENDING-CITATION |

**Ambiguity notes**

- THE SCALE TRAP, and it is the sharpest one here BECAUSE the Latin is genuinely CITED. Classical membrana is a TISSUE-SCALE object you could see and peel: Cicero's 'natura oculos membranis tenuissimis vestivit' is about the coats of the eye. The concept is a MOLECULAR lipid bilayer roughly 5 nm thick, whose defining properties are lipid physics and selective permeability. A fully-sourced classical citation can still be the wrong referent, and here it is: L&S carries the word, and the word does not carry the chemistry. An entry can be CITED and still not mean what you need it to mean -- this file's own worked example of that. ('A perfect classical citation' was the original wording; 'perfect' is banned in author voice by the same charter rule 18.14 this file invokes in not_claimed, and the word was doing rhetorical work here that the evidence does not need.)
- membrana's transferred classical sense is 'parchment' (L&S, citing Quintilian and Horace). Parchment is a DEAD, PROCESSED, IMPERMEABLE sheet. That is the near-exact inverse of a selectively permeable living boundary, and it is a sense a classically-trained reader carries as live.
- THE FREIGHT THE DEFINITION ITSELF GUARDS: the concept's own definition says the membrane's satisfying I(mu;eta|b) = 0 is a DIFFERENT question whose answer is NOT-MEASURED. So no register may be chosen because it suggests boundary-hood in the blanket sense. The corpus's note on this concept is blunt -- 'the observation that organisms have surfaces is not evidence that the surface is a Markov blanket' -- and it names the rule: do not let a membrane and a blanket be rendered with one term. Whatever renders MARKOV_BLANKET, it must not be tvac and must not be membrana.
- tvac's ritual register is live and specific: MW carries 'a cow's hide used in Soma pressing' and 'a leather bag' (RV. v, 33, 7). The word arrives carrying sacrificial equipment. It also carries 'darkness (as black cover)' and 'a mystical name for the letter ya', either of which will read as deliberate symbolism to a Sanskritist encountering it in a technical document.
- tvac means bark as readily as skin. Bark is dead secondary tissue. If the rendering is read botanically, the referent becomes a dead structural layer -- again the inverse of the living, selectively permeable object.

**Forbidden mistranslations**

Phylogenetic inertia, drift, developmental constraint, pleiotropy and historical contingency are five DIFFERENT causes, each producing non-adaptive features by a different route. A register that renders them as 'chance' or 'accident' collapses five mechanisms into one and destroys the argument's force -- drift is stochastic, but developmental constraint and pleiotropy are not chance at all.
- 'Not optimal solutions to anything' is stronger than 'suboptimal' and the difference is the point. A suboptimal solution is still a solution to some problem. The claim is that some features solve NOTHING -- they are byproducts, inheritances, or side-effects. A register that renders it as 'imperfect adaptation' has conceded the adaptationist premise while appearing to state the objection to it.
- The concept is META store: it disciplines commentary, and is never itself a TRUE signal. It cannot be falsified by a measurement of an organism, because it is not a claim about any organism -- it is a claim about what may be inferred from organisms.

**Forbidden mistranslations**

| register | form | why it is wrong |
|---|---|---|
|  |  | Imports a standard nature is failing to meet, and hence a designer with intentions who erred. The claim is that some features are not solutions to anything AT ALL -- not that they are failed solutions. 'Mistake' presupposes an attempt. |
|  |  | Makes it detachable. CONCEPTS.json says it is the MANDATORY companion and that it travels with nature-as-authority EVERYWHERE. An objection is something one may answer and move past; a counterweight is structural and always present. The wrong word here would let the whole discipline be dropped politely. |
|  |  | Only drift is stochastic. Phylogenetic inertia is history, developmental constraint is mechanism, pleiotropy is genetic architecture, contingency is path-dependence. Collapsing them concedes that non-adaptive features are mere noise -- which is exactly the adaptationist reply the argument is built to block. |
|  |  | Overshoots in the other direction. CONCEPTS.json's gate is precise: a nature-derived design must beat a tuned baseline on a pre-registered metric or be recorded NEGATIVE. That gate is 'the entire difference between this wing and cargo-cult biomimicry' -- it disciplines the method, it does not abolish it. |

**Back-translation test** — status: `NOT-RUN (no candidate)`

pages.body:
# The lexicon — every concept, by domain

> **RENDERED FROM STRUCTURED DATA — this page is not a markdown file.**
> Source: `lexicon/CONCEPTS.json` in `uni-cookbook` at `575fc93d9d31`.
> The sha256 recorded for this page is the digest of **that JSON**, not of this text. The
> renderer is `generators/derive_docs.cjs`; it copies fields and adds no facts. Every value
> below is a field of the source, verbatim, including the ones that read `NOT RUN` and `PENDING`.


The canonical concept list: the backbone of the five-register lexicon (Sanskrit / Latin / English / Hindi / Spanish). Each entry fixes ONE concept by its DEFINITION, not by its word. The definition is the translatable object and the test object: a candidate rendering in any register is admissible only if it back-translates to a sentence that preserves this definition's discriminating property, and a translator is tested on the definition, never on the headword. NOTHING HERE IS TRANSLATED YET. This file carries no Sanskrit, Latin, Hindi, or Spanish, and asserts no equivalence in any register; per rule 18.14 of the operator's own charter ('Do not claim perfect translation'), every future rendering enters PENDING / SUB EXAMINE and is admitted only against a cited dictionary headword plus a passing back-translation test. Sanskrit technical vocabulary for modern math and physics largely DOES NOT EXIST as attested classical terms; the honest expectation is many coined entries, recorded as coinages, and no attested word may be pretended to mean 'expected free energy'. Sanskrit philosophical vocabulary carries DOCTRINAL FREIGHT (a Samkhya or Vedanta term imports a metaphysics); the ambiguity_notes of the future register files, not this file, are where that is recorded, and no translation choice may quietly assert a metaphysics. The 'store' field routes each concept to its sovereign store and is NEVER a claim about the concept's truth: TRUE = the concept names something falsifiable/reproducible/recalibratable; HONEST = it names lived experience, which is never calibrated; META = it names commentary about signals, which travels separately and is never True. Two counts are load-bearing and are reported here rather than discovered later: GENERATIVE_PROCESS appears in 0 files of this corpus (grep, 2026-07-15) and is introduced here because the model/process conflation is the field's most-confused pair; META appears in 0 files of this corpus and is carried from the wider UNI Tree doctrine (arca META), not from anything the encyclopedia says. This file is a lexicon backbone. It raises no UNI rung, discharges no gate, and states no fact about nature. A nature citation is never a UNI gate.

**Field contract** — [object Object]

## active-inference-math — 29

| concept | English | definition |
|---|---|---|
| `ACTIVE_INFERENCE` | active inference | A scheme in which perception minimizes variational free energy over beliefs and action minimizes expected free energy over policies, so that perceiving and acting are one operation applied through the two halves of a blanket. |
| `VARIATIONAL_FREE_ENERGY` | variational free energy | A scalar functional F[q,o] = E_q(s)[ln q(s) - ln p(o,s)], in nats, that scores a belief q(s) against observations o and upper-bounds surprisal, so minimizing it over q both drives q toward the true posterior and tightens the bound. |
| `EXPECTED_FREE_ENERGY` | expected free energy | A scalar G(pi), in nats, that scores a candidate policy rather than a belief, equal to risk plus ambiguity and equivalently to the negative sum of epistemic and pragmatic value, so that the lowest-G policy is the chosen one. |
| `SURPRISAL` | surprisal | The self-information -ln p(o) of an observation under a model, measuring how unexpected that observation was, in nats, and being the quantity that variational free energy upper-bounds. |
| `GENERATIVE_MODEL` | generative model | The joint distribution p(o,s) that an agent HOLDS over observations and hidden states, specifying how states are believed to cause observations and how states are believed to evolve, and which is a choice the agent makes rather than a measurement of the world. |
| `GENERATIVE_PROCESS` | generative process | The actual dynamics of the world that really produce observations, which exist independently of any agent's beliefs and need not share the generative model's form, variables, or factorization. |
| `RECOGNITION_DENSITY` | recognition density (approximate posterior q) | The distribution q(s) that is an agent's honest and improvable belief over hidden states, being the object optimized during perception and generally NOT equal to the true posterior. |
| `TRUE_POSTERIOR` | true posterior | The exact conditional p(s\|o) implied by the generative model, generally intractable because it requires the marginal p(o) = SUM_s p(o,s), and which q approximates without necessarily ever equalling. |
| `BOUND_GAP` | bound gap | The non-negative slack D_KL[q(s)\|\|p(s\|o)] between variational free energy and surprisal, which is zero exactly when q equals the true posterior and is unobservable without the very posterior that was intractable to begin with. |
| `ACCURACY` | accuracy | The term E_q(s)[ln p(o\|s)] in F's complexity-minus-accuracy decomposition, measuring how well a belief explains the observations actually received. |
| `COMPLEXITY` | complexity | The term D_KL[q(s)\|\|p(s)] in F, measuring how far a belief has moved off its prior and penalizing that movement so that minimizing F selects the simplest sufficient explanation rather than the best fit. |
| `KL_DIVERGENCE` | Kullback-Leibler divergence | A non-negative measure of the difference between two distributions, zero if and only if they are equal (Gibbs' inequality), whose non-negativity is precisely what makes F upper-bound surprisal. |
| `ENTROPY` | entropy | The expected surprisal H of a distribution, measuring the average uncertainty of outcomes drawn from it, in nats. |
| `EVIDENCE` | evidence (marginal likelihood) | The marginal p(o) = SUM_s p(o,s) of observations under a model, whose negative logarithm is surprisal and whose logarithm F lower-bounds in negated form. |
| `NAT` | nat | The unit of information under natural logarithms, equal to log2(e) or about 1.442695 bits, in which F, G, entropy and surprisal are all measured. |
| `RISK` | risk | The divergence D_KL[q(o\|pi)\|\|p(o\|C)] between a policy's predicted outcomes and its preferred outcomes, forming one of the two terms of expected free energy. |
| `AMBIGUITY` | ambiguity | The expected entropy of the likelihood, E_q(s\|pi)[H[p(o\|s)]], measuring how uninformative observations will be even if the policy reaches the states it intends. |
| `EPISTEMIC_VALUE` | epistemic value | The expected information gain of a policy, being the expected divergence between the belief that would be held after observing and the belief held now, which minimizing G maximizes. |
| `PRAGMATIC_VALUE` | pragmatic value | The expected log-preference E_q(o\|pi)[ln p(o\|C)] of a policy, measuring how far its predicted outcomes move the agent toward its preferred observations. |
| `POLICY` | policy | A candidate action sequence pi over which expected free energy is scored and among which one is selected. |
| `POLICY_PRECISION` | policy precision (gamma) | The inverse-temperature parameter gamma > 0, carrying units of inverse nats, that sharpens the softmax over policies, with gamma approaching 0 giving indifference and gamma approaching infinity giving deterministic argmin G. |
| `PRECISION` | precision | The confidence weighting on a distribution or signal, formally the inverse variance or the inverse-covariance (precision) matrix, which sets how strongly a term is allowed to drive inference. |
| `PRIOR` | prior | The distribution p(s) held over hidden states before the current observation is taken into account. |
| `PREFERENCE` | preference (C) | A prior p(o\|C) over PREFERRED observations that encodes a goal as a distribution rather than as a reward signal, and which breaks the tie between revising beliefs and acting on the world. |
| `LIKELIHOOD` | likelihood | The mapping p(o\|s) from hidden states to observations, realized as the A tensor in a discrete POMDP. |
| `TRANSITION` | transition | The mapping p(s'\|s,u) from a current hidden state and an action to the next hidden state, realized as the B tensor in a discrete POMDP. |
| `ELBO` | evidence lower bound (ELBO) | The negative of variational free energy, being a lower bound on the log evidence ln p(o), such that maximizing it is identical to minimizing F. |
| `FREE_ENERGY_PRINCIPLE` | free energy principle | The proposal that self-organizing systems at non-equilibrium steady state minimize a variational free-energy bound on surprisal, which designates a MODEL STRUCTURE rather than an empirical finding. |
| `ACTION_AS_INFERENCE` | action as inference | The consequence of the blanket partition that a prediction error can be resolved either by changing internal states to fit the world or by changing active states until the world fits the model, both minimizing the same quantity. |

## sovereign-vocabulary — 27

| concept | English | definition |
|---|---|---|
| `TRUE_SIGNAL` | TRUE signal | A signal that is falsifiable, reproducible and recalibratable, with every calibration present and prior recorded, such that if it cannot be falsified or reproduced it is not True. |
| `HONEST_SIGNAL` | HONEST signal | Lived experience, respected exactly as lived and NEVER calibrated, which is not a failed measurement but a different kind of signal, and whose lack of a falsifier is the point rather than a gap. |
| `META_SIGNAL` | META signal | Commentary about a signal, which travels separately from the signal itself and is never True. |
| `SOVEREIGN_ISOLATION` | sovereign isolation | The rule that TRUE and HONEST signals keep separate stores, separate ledgers and separate Merkle roots, and that crossing them is the cardinal sin. |
| `SIGNUM_SIGNUM_MANET` | the signal remains the signal | The doctrine that the signal and the commentary about it travel separately, so that an attribution is never merged into the value it describes. |
| `RES_IPSAE_NON_SIMULACRA` | the things themselves, not simulacra | The doctrine that no value, citation, URL, DOI or dictionary entry is ever fabricated: source it, or write NOT-MEASURED, and there is no third state. |
| `CARDINAL_RULE` | the cardinal rule | A nature citation is never a UNI gate: reading Kleiber's law raises no UNI rung, and no operation takes a NATURA row and a UNI row and produces a stronger row of either kind. |
| `UNI_FENCE` | the UNI four-value fence | The vocabulary proven / designed / hypothesized / not-yet-built that governs UNI's own build status and is never used of nature. |
| `PROVEN` | proven | A held, sealed, UNI-signed PASS (Class A or C) with its falsifier still live -- a status of UNI's own artifact passing UNI's own gate, and reserved for the UNI ledger. |
| `DESIGNED` | designed | A typed spec or signed-in-principle design exists while the build is partial or unverified, which raises nothing and leaves the rung's status unchanged. |
| `HYPOTHESIZED_UNI` | hypothesized (UNI fence value) | A stated UNI mechanism with no sealed gate yet (Class U), not claimed. |
| `NOT_YET_BUILT` | not-yet-built | No engine, no run, no gate: an absence in UNI's build, hard-fenced as north-star framing. |
| `NATURA_CLASS` | NATURA evidence class | The twelve-class, three-group vocabulary (measured / derived / fenced) that governs nature's observed regularities and is never merged with the UNI four. |
| `OBSERVED_REPLICATED` | OBSERVED-REPLICATED | Measured and independently replicated across labs, datasets or taxa, carrying a real citation, a falsifier and the known range. |
| `OBSERVED_SINGLE` | OBSERVED-SINGLE | Measured by a method another party could repeat, but with NO independent replication on record, asserting the measurement and asserting nothing whatever about corroboration. |
| `OBSERVED_CONTESTED` | OBSERVED-CONTESTED | Measured, but with the community genuinely disputing the value, the exponent or the mechanism, so that both positions must be carried and the dispute named. |
| `MODELED` | MODELED | Derived from a model that fits data, where the model's ASSUMPTIONS are the fence and must be cited with it. |
| `MODELED_CONTESTED` | MODELED-CONTESTED | Derived from a model AND genuinely disputed by the community, so the row must survive both tests rather than one. |
| `HYPOTHESIZED_NATURA` | HYPOTHESIZED (NATURA class) | A mechanism about nature that is proposed but not settled, and is not claimed. |
| `INADMISSIBLE` | INADMISSIBLE | A claim that failed observation, or that is unfalsifiable as stated, carried WITH the receipt of why it failed -- never asserted, never mocked. |
| `SUPERSEDED` | SUPERSEDED | A value that was carried in the literature and has since been retracted, withdrawn by its own authors, or contradicted by a calibrated re-analysis, kept as the receipt for why it must not be cited. |
| `NOT_MEASURED` | NOT-MEASURED | The honest empty face: nobody has measured it -- an absence in the literature, written instead of inventing a number. |
| `NOT_SOURCED` | NOT-SOURCED | The chapter states a value it could not trace to a source: somebody measured it, and this corpus could not find who. |
| `NOT_CONFIRMED` | NOT-CONFIRMED | The primary source is named at one remove -- a secondary or tertiary work cites it -- but the primary was not read in this pass, so the provenance chain is known and unwalked. |
| `NOT_LOCATED` | NOT-LOCATED | A named source was searched for and does not appear to exist -- the strongest of the three provenance fences. |
| `QUAESTIO_APERTA` | open question | A permanent open question -- 'full human' and 'the next evolution beyond human' -- which is never a target, never a milestone, and never a deliverable. |
| `NONDUM_FALSIFICABILIS` | not yet falsifiable | A REGISTER STATUS and not an evidence class: the mark of an item held in the open-questions register, outside the Tree, which is read and not acted upon. |

## method — 21

| concept | English | definition |
|---|---|---|
| `FALSIFIER` | falsifier | A stated observation that would refute a claim, written before the run, without which surprise cannot be computed and the claim is inadmissible. |
| `RECEIPT` | receipt | The captured observation that closes a turn of the loop -- an audit id and UTC for live state, file:line for code, a run log for tests -- against which the prior prediction is compared. |
| `EVIDENCE_CLASS` | evidence class | The A-to-U label recording HOW a claim is known, above which no claim may ever be raised. |
| `CLASS_AUTHORITY_ORDERING` | class authority ordering | M9's rule that Class-B tool state overrides Class-G own narrative and Class-A runtime observation overrides Class-E test pass, so that a passing test does NOT satisfy a criterion demanding a runtime observation. |
| `LEDGER` | ledger | The append-only single source of truth whose four states are PASS, FAIL, NEGATIVE and PENDING, and which wins wherever prose disagrees with it. |
| `CALIBRATION` | calibration | Moving wording DOWN to the measured value -- never up -- and keeping the prior wording on record, so that the fence gets louder under pressure rather than wider. |
| `NEGATIVE` | negative | A held UNI run that missed its pre-registered bar: a result UNI earned, published front-and-center as the credibility, and never retried until it wins. |
| `BASELINE` | tuned baseline | A strong comparison tuned with the same effort spent on the method itself, since an untuned baseline measures the author's enthusiasm rather than the mechanism. |
| `DISCRIMINATOR` | load-bearing discriminator | A manipulation -- shuffling labels, swapping markers, ablating the mechanism to zero -- that must COLLAPSE the claimed gain, since a gain surviving the destruction of its own mechanism was never the mechanism's. |
| `ABLATION` | ablation | Removal of a mechanism in order to measure its contribution, whose number must be a computed residual and never a literal typed in by hand. |
| `PRE_REGISTRATION` | pre-registration | Writing the bar, the margin, the threshold, the named ablation and the stopping rule BEFORE the build, because reasonable data-contingent analytic choices inflate false positives with no deliberate p-hacking at all. |
| `HELD_SET` | held set | Data touched exactly ONCE behind a seal-before-scoring step and a once-only sentinel, since a held set scored twice is a training set with a good reputation. |
| `BOUND_NOT_POINT` | the bound, not the point estimate | M2's verdict rule: the verdict is the confidence-interval bound that EXCLUDES the threshold, never the point estimate. |
| `SEVERITY` | severity | Mayo's requirement that a passing test counts as evidence only if it could have failed, made operable as the single question: if the claim were false, what is the probability this exact procedure would still have passed it? |
| `STRONG_INFERENCE` | strong inference | Platt's procedure of devising alternative hypotheses, devising a crucial experiment each of whose possible outcomes EXCLUDES one or more of them, carrying it out to a clean result, and recycling. |
| `MULTIPLE_WORKING_HYPOTHESES` | multiple working hypotheses | Chamberlin's remedy of plurality rather than neutrality: keep at least two hypotheses always and at least three for anything you intend to claim, each structurally distinct in mechanism rather than in parameter. |
| `REPLICATION` | replication | Independent repetition of a measurement by another party, whose presence or absence is exactly what separates OBSERVED-REPLICATED from OBSERVED-SINGLE. |
| `ANOMALY` | anomaly | A residual that survives the hunt for instrument error -- stable, isotropic-or-not, and quantitatively characterized -- which is the most valuable object in science and the seed of the trajectory nuisance to residual to characterized anomaly to discriminating test to precision measurement. |
| `POSITIVE_CONTROL` | positive control | A run proving the instrument can detect the effect it is looking for, without which a negative result is a hypothesis rather than a finding. |
| `PROVENANCE` | provenance | The record of what was measured, on what instrument, by whom, when, and through which cable, kept well enough that the loose connector can be found. |
| `CAVITY_PRINCIPLE` | the cavity principle | M22's rule that a hierarchy level must never treat an upstream prior as fresh evidence, but must divide it out. |

## natura — 20

| concept | English | definition |
|---|---|---|
| `NATURE_AS_AUTHORITY` | nature as the authority | The doctrine, defensible in exactly one form, that nature is authoritative because it is the only system that has already run the experiment -- a very long parallel search under real physical constraints in which the failures were deleted. |
| `ADAPTATIONIST_COUNTERWEIGHT` | the adaptationist counterweight | Gould & Lewontin's mandatory companion to nature-as-authority: not every trait is an adaptation, because phylogenetic inertia, drift, developmental constraint, pleiotropy and historical contingency all produce features that are not optimal solutions to anything. |
| `CONVERGENT_EVOLUTION` | convergent evolution | Independent lineages arriving at the same solution, which is EVIDENCE of a constraint-optimum and never proof of one. |
| `CONSTRAINT_OPTIMUM` | constraint-optimum | A solution repeatedly rediscovered by independent lineages under real physical constraints, which is what convergent evolution is evidence of. |
| `RATIO` | ratio | A quotient of two measured quantities, which usually does NOT survive a change of scale and which must carry its scope, units and class to be admissible. |
| `DIMENSIONLESS_NUMBER` | dimensionless number | A quotient whose units cancel, which travels across scale precisely because it does, and which is therefore the group to read before any ratio. |
| `REYNOLDS_NUMBER` | Reynolds number | Re = rho*v*L/mu = v*L/nu, the ratio of inertial to viscous forces, which spans about thirteen orders of magnitude from bacterium to whale and across which the physics of swimming changes IDENTITY rather than degree. |
| `SCALING_LAW` | scaling law | A power law fitted within a regime, whose exponent stops being a fact about the world at a regime boundary and which does not extrapolate through one. |
| `ALLOMETRY` | allometry | The scaling of a biological quantity with body mass, canonically BMR proportional to M^b, whose exponent moves with analysis choices and changes at the major evolutionary transitions. |
| `REGIME_BOUNDARY` | regime boundary | The point at which the dominant dimensionless group moves by orders of magnitude or the dominant force changes identity, past which a fitted exponent does not carry. |
| `SCALE_LADDER` | the scale ladder | The sixteen-rung sequence from quark to galaxy ordered by characteristic length, on which Markov blankets appear at the organelle, cell and organism rungs and vanish above and below. |
| `RUNG` | rung | A level that exists only when all three of these hold: a boundary with real conditional independence forms, a characteristic timescale separates from the level below, and the level has its own dynamics that do not require tracking the level below. |
| `EMERGENCE` | emergence | A statement about spectral gaps in a dynamical system: timescale separation makes a level's own dynamics writable without tracking the level below, so that broken symmetry at each level generates concepts not present in the level below. |
| `FREQUENCY` | frequency | A rate of repetition in hertz, admissible only with its measurand and scope, since values landing in the same numeric neighbourhood may be entirely different physics. |
| `RESONANCE` | resonance | The selective amplification of a driven system near a characteristic frequency of a real cavity or oscillator, which licenses the frequency and nothing attached to the frequency. |
| `DIFFUSION` | diffusion | Transport by random thermal motion, whose characteristic time scales as the square of distance and which therefore fails as a delivery mechanism above a characteristic length. |
| `GRADIENT` | gradient | A spatial variation of a quantity, which is a measured object at one rung and a rhetorical one across rungs unless the measurand, its units, and two rungs measured with it are all stated. |
| `MORPHOGENESIS` | morphogenesis | The generation of form from local rules during growth, in which pattern arises without a blueprint. |
| `CELL` | cell | The design unit of biology and the canonical Markov blanket, plasma-membrane bounded and dominated by viscosity and diffusion at Re of order 1e-5. |
| `MEMBRANE` | membrane | A selectively permeable lipid boundary, which is a surface for reasons of lipid physics and history, and whose satisfying I(mu;eta\|b) = 0 is a DIFFERENT question whose answer is NOT-MEASURED. |

## markov-blanket — 14

| concept | English | definition |
|---|---|---|
| `MARKOV_BLANKET` | Markov blanket | The set b = {s,a} of sensory and active states whose conditioning renders internal and external states independent, so that p(mu,eta\|b) = p(mu\|b)p(eta\|b), equivalently I(mu;eta\|b) = 0. |
| `MIND` | mind (internal states, mu) | The internal states mu inside a blanket, which have no term in external states and whose only evidence about the world is the sensory states. |
| `BODY` | body (the blanket, b) | The blanket b = {s,a} itself: the surface that carries every dependency between mind and world, and that thereby determines what is inferable at all. |
| `MIND_BODY` | mind.body (the interface) | The coupling mu to b -- a pair of one-way doors, sensory states the world's only route in and active states the mind's only route out -- which is not a fifth thing but the interface itself. |
| `WORLD` | world (external states, eta) | The external states eta outside the blanket, which a mind reaches exactly never and which enter only as a hypothesis that explains the blanket. |
| `SENSORY_STATES` | sensory states | The blanket states s influenced by external but not internal states, forming the world's only route into the mind. |
| `ACTIVE_STATES` | active states | The blanket states a influenced by internal but not external states, forming the mind's only route out into the world. |
| `CONDITIONAL_INDEPENDENCE` | conditional independence | The relation mu perp eta given b, which is the whole content of a blanket: given the blanket, internal and external states carry no further information about each other. |
| `CONDITIONAL_MUTUAL_INFORMATION` | conditional mutual information | The quantity I(mu;eta\|b), in nats, which is the operable test of whether a candidate boundary is a real blanket, since I greater than zero beyond estimator noise means a route from world to mind bypasses the body and the partition is drawn in the wrong place. |
| `PEARL_BLANKET` | Pearl blanket | A blanket as Pearl coined it: a formal statistical construct over a graph you drew, doing conditional-independence bookkeeping relative to a model, and thereby cheap, well-defined and unobjectionable. |
| `FRISTON_BLANKET` | Friston blanket | A blanket read as the metaphysical boundary of a real thing -- the claim that some system out there genuinely has an inside, a surface and an outside -- which requires premises beyond the formalism's mathematical success. |
| `BLANKET_SLIDE` | the Pearl-to-Friston slide | The field's characteristic error of defining a Pearl blanket, which is free, and then quietly concluding one has discovered where the organism ends, which is expensive and requires a measurement nobody made. |
| `INTEROCEPTION` | interoception | Sensory channels whose external states are other parts of the same organism, forming a blanket nested inside a blanket, and rendered in M12's engineering clause as hardware signals. |
| `BLANKET_NESTING` | blanket nesting | The recursion in which one level's blanket becomes part of the next level's internal states, running organelle to cell to tissue to organ to organism to colony to ecosystem. |

## pomdp-tensors — 9

| concept | English | definition |
|---|---|---|
| `POMDP` | partially observable Markov decision process | A discrete formalism of hidden states, observations and actions in which states are not directly visible, over which this corpus's engine runs the loop perceive, EFE-plan, act, learn. |
| `A_TENSOR` | A tensor (likelihood) | The tensor encoding p(o\|s), mapping hidden states to observations, and one of the four tensors this corpus's engine learns by conjugate-Dirichlet counts. |
| `B_TENSOR` | B tensor (transition) | The tensor encoding p(s'\|s,u), mapping a hidden state and an action to the next hidden state, and one of the four tensors learned by conjugate-Dirichlet counts. |
| `C_TENSOR` | C tensor (preferences) | The tensor encoding the prior p(o\|C) over preferred observations, which -- alone among A, B, C, D and E -- is SET rather than learned by Dirichlet counts, being fixed in this corpus by the Z affect modulator. |
| `D_TENSOR` | D tensor (initial state prior) | The tensor encoding the prior over hidden states at the start of a trial or episode, and one of the four tensors learned by conjugate-Dirichlet counts. |
| `E_TENSOR` | E tensor (habits / policy prior) | The tensor encoding the prior over policies, biasing policy selection before any expected-free-energy score is computed, and one of the four tensors learned by conjugate-Dirichlet counts. |
| `DIRICHLET_LEARNING` | conjugate Dirichlet learning | The exact update of the A, B, D and E tensors by counts + lr * sufficient_stat, which is conjugate and therefore requires no gradient, no autodiff, and no backpropagation. |
| `HIDDEN_STATE` | hidden state | The quantity s that an agent cannot observe directly and must infer, and about which the recognition density is a belief. |
| `OBSERVATION` | observation | The quantity o that actually arrived at the sensor, which is what a belief is scored against and what a receipt records. |

## build-objects — 7

| concept | English | definition |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENT` | agent | A system that holds a generative model and minimizes free energy through a blanket, concerning which nothing further is implied: a system that minimizes F is a system that minimizes F. |
| `ORGAN` | organ | A named instrument built to run one loop, carrying its own harness, and durable only once committed rather than once deployed. |
| `ORGANISM` | organism | The scale-ladder rung at which a Markov blanket is identifiable, gravity enters as a dominant constraint, and metabolic rate scales with body mass within its regime. |
| `HIERARCHY` | hierarchy | Nested levels each of whose blanket becomes part of the next level's internal states, made reachable by evolution because stable intermediates are what interruption spares. |
| `WORLD_COUPLING` | world coupling | The interface by which an engine's internal states are exposed to a world, isolated by explicit whitelist rather than by blacklist. |
| `Z_MODULATOR` | the Z affect modulator | The global vector of energy, arousal, valence, fatigue, pain, threat, safety and inflammation that sets precision, preferences, habits, learning rate and horizon. |
| `SENSORIUM` | sensorium | A body-to-mind categorical observation interface whose modality count is an empirical question, kept at seven because an over-compressed two-modality bottleneck went NEGATIVE on held data. |

## world-context — 3

| concept | English | definition |
|---|---|---|
| `GAIA` | Gaia | The claim that the biosphere homeostatically regulates the planet, which is HYPOTHESIZED as regulation with a live unanswered unit-of-selection objection, and INADMISSIBLE as the literal claim that the Earth is an organism. |
| `LABORATORY` | laboratory | The bounded setting in which a pre-registered metric and a tuned baseline decide a design, and whose engineering or substrate evidence is never general evidence about the science. |
| `TOY_WORLD` | toy world | The honest scope of this whole program: a developmental active-inference SIMULATION, a bounded peek, a toy world, and never a person. |
